title: Who buys, who receives and who keeps the books?
lead: A buyer can negotiate for two factories while each factory keeps its own inventory. The fields on a purchasing document describe different responsibilities, so two organizational codes that look similar can have very different effects.
sections: Draw the assignments

A company code represents a unit of financial accounting. A plant identifies an operational location, and a storage location distinguishes stocks within a plant. A purchasing organization negotiates and procures for its assigned plants. A purchasing group identifies the buyer or buying team. Record who owns each decision before assigning codes. A purchasing group can handle a family of materials across plants even though each plant is assigned to a single company code.
Follow a shared negotiation

A group has factories East and West in different company codes. A central team negotiates a common bearing price. A cross-company purchasing organization can support both plants when the assignments allow it. East orders 100 bearings for East, while West orders 50 for West. A common negotiator does not pool their physical stock or move their invoices into one legal entity. On each order, verify the ordering company code, plant at item level, and purchasing organization.
Find the level that failed

If a buyer can create an order for East but cannot select West, compare the two organizational assignment paths and the vendor’s purchasing data for the actual organization. If another buyer can use exactly the same combination, capture that difference for an authorization investigation. Extending a material at a plant solves a different problem from assigning a purchasing organization to that plant. Identify the failing relationship before requesting master-data changes.

title: Where does SAP value a material?
lead: A physical address answers where an item sits. A valuation area answers where SAP maintains its financial valuation. Distinguishing those questions explains why two bins can share one price and two plants can have different prices for the same material.
sections: Separate the stock address from the valuation address

In classic ERP, the valuation level is set at plant or company-code level for the system. At plant level each plant is a valuation area. At company-code level the plants of that company code share a valuation area. A storage location provides a quantity breakdown within a plant. Under ordinary single valuation, creating another storage location does not establish another valuation price. Check the implemented valuation level before treating a price difference as an error.
Reconstruct the opening picture

Plant A holds 30 units in Stores and 20 in Dispatch at a standard price of 10, with a price unit of one. Plant B holds 50 at 12. With plant valuation the two stocks are worth 500 and 600 respectively. Moving five unrestricted units from Stores to Dispatch within Plant A leaves A with 50 units worth 500. A report grouped by storage location changes even though the valuation-area total stays constant.
Explain a difference before changing a price

Compare the material, valuation area, currency, price unit, price control, valuation type where used and posting period. A displayed price of 1,000 per 100 pieces and a price of 10 per piece describe the same rate. If comparing a transfer between plants, establish whether the plants sit in different valuation areas and what process was posted. A storage-location transfer example alone cannot predict the accounting treatment of a cross-plant movement.

title: A material exists, but can this plant use it?
lead: A material number can appear in search results while a plant still lacks data needed to plan, purchase or value it. A material master contains both shared descriptions and records for specific organizational levels.
sections: Read the key behind the screen

Basic data such as the description and base unit identifies the material across the client. Plant data can carry local planning and purchasing settings. Valuation data belongs to the valuation area, and storage locations distinguish local stock. A material view is a business grouping of fields. The organizational key behind each field determines how widely changing it can affect the business. The set of views needed depends on the business process and material type.
Test an extension request

A repair shop adds Plant B to a bearing already purchased in Plant A. The code and base unit match, but B uses a different receiving lead time and its own planning parameters. Extend the existing material to the relevant levels, using A only as a starting point. Review local fields with their owners. For a valuated stock purchase, also confirm valuation data for B’s valuation area. A description search succeeding does not demonstrate that a goods receipt can post.
Use a smallest useful comparison

Display the same material in both plants with identical views and compare the fields required by the intended transaction. Check material status and any restrictions alongside missing data. Then run one business example in QA with the intended plant, purchasing organization and account assignment. Keep the error message, the organizational levels used and the field changed. This makes the result reusable when the next material fails at a different level.

title: Why can Purchasing use a vendor that Finance cannot pay?
lead: Classic ERP vendor data spans several organizational levels. Being able to find a vendor by name proves very little about whether a particular company code can post an invoice or a purchasing organization can place an order.
sections: Follow the responsibilities

General vendor data identifies the business partner across the client. Company-code data supports financial accounting and includes the reconciliation account used for the vendor subledger. Purchasing-organization data holds purchasing defaults such as order currency and commercial settings. The business can also maintain partner roles where its purchasing process requires them. A separate invoicing party or goods supplier can therefore matter even when a buyer recognizes the ordering address.
Work the two-company example

Vendor 4100 supplies gloves to two factories. The buyer can select the vendor in purchasing organization P100, and company code 1000 has the financial master data. When company code 2000 goes live, reusing vendor number 4100 retains the shared identity. Its existing 1000 record does not supply the missing company-code data for 2000. Conversely, maintaining financial data for 2000 alone cannot establish all purchasing defaults for a new purchasing organization.
Localize the fault

Capture the failing document, organization and partner number before comparing master records. For an invoice problem, identify the invoicing party and company code. For a PO default problem, identify the ordering vendor and purchasing organization. Inspect blocks and deletion flags at the relevant levels. A bank or payment complaint can involve additional controls in Finance. Hand Finance the exact partner, legal entity and document reference so they can test the right record.

title: Read a purchase as a chain of evidence
lead: A request, an order, a delivery and an invoice answer different questions. Following their references at item level lets you tell where a transaction stands even when users say simply that their purchase is “complete.”
sections: Start with the strength of each document

A purchase requisition records internal demand. A purchase order records the instruction to a supplier. A goods receipt records a posted receiving event. A supplier invoice records the financial claim entered in invoice verification. A vendor payment is a later Finance event. Document creation, approval, output, physical arrival and posting are separate events with potentially different dates. Use the document that evidences the specific business claim a colleague is making.
Read a partial chain

A requester asks for 100 cases. The buyer orders 80 from one supplier. The warehouse posts 60 against PO item 10. Accounts Payable posts an invoice for 50. In this simplified example all documents use cases and no reversals exist. There are 20 requested cases outside that PO, 20 ordered cases still to receive, and 10 received cases beyond the invoiced quantity. Adding those three differences would produce a meaningless total because each answers a different question.
Trace both directions

From the order item, display its purchase order history and open the material and invoice documents. Trace the original PR item reference separately. Review returns, cancellations, units and posting dates before concluding that something is missing. For invoices relating to several items, compare each item separately. An invoice posted against a vendor does not by itself establish that a particular PO item was invoiced. A payment question belongs with Finance once the invoice reference is known.

title: A carton, a piece and a price per hundred
lead: Three quantities can appear on one purchase order without contradicting each other. The order unit describes how the supplier delivers, the base unit supports inventory, and the price can be quoted in another unit and for a multiple of that unit.
sections: Write down the dimensions

Record the order unit, order price unit, conversion factors, currency and numerical price unit. In the expression “240 per 100 pieces,” pieces is the order price unit and 100 is the numerical price unit. If the buyer orders cartons, convert cartons to pieces before multiplying by the price. A material or supplier-specific conversion matters because another supplier may pack the same material in differently sized cartons.
Calculate the expected amount

A buyer orders five cartons with twelve pieces per carton. The supplier quotes 240 per hundred pieces in the PO currency. Five cartons contain sixty pieces. Sixty divided by one hundred, multiplied by 240, gives 144 before taxes, freight or discounts. A partial delivery of three cartons represents thirty-six pieces. At the same rate its simple goods value is 86.40. Write the unit after each intermediate quantity so an inverted ratio is easy to spot.
Investigate a factor-of-ten difference

Compare the conversion stored on the actual PO item with the quotation and current master records. A correct current master record alone cannot demonstrate which conversion was saved on an older order. Confirm the invoiced quantity’s unit, price denominator and currency. If the material uses a variable relationship such as pieces purchased by actual weight, a fixed carton example will not establish the invoiced weight. Obtain the measured delivery quantity used by the document.

title: Why can the warehouse see stock but not issue it?
lead: A stock figure answers a question about a particular owner, location and condition. Two people can quote different quantities for the same material and both be reading the system correctly.
sections: Define what you are counting

Start with the material, plant, storage location, batch where relevant, and the time of the snapshot. Separate unrestricted-use, quality inspection and blocked stock. The warehouse may physically hold all three. A normal issue from unrestricted stock needs quantity in that bucket. A quality inspection process may require a usage decision before release. The material master base unit is the safest unit for comparing the stock overview, material documents and physical count.
Work the warehouse call

Assume the company owns 100 cartons in one location. Sixty are unrestricted, 30 are in quality inspection and ten are blocked. An issue of 75 from unrestricted stock is short by 15. If Quality authorizes release of 20 and the stock posting is completed, unrestricted stock becomes 80. The same 75-carton issue would leave five unrestricted, ten in inspection and ten blocked. Only the issue reduces the location total. A stock-type change explains how availability can rise while physical quantity stays constant.
Trace a disagreement

Open the stock overview for the precise combination used at issue. Compare its base unit and stock type with the failed item, then follow the most recent stock-type transfer and any inspection lot. Distinguish ordinary blocked stock from a conditional 103 receipt into GR blocked stock. The latter records a pending acceptance in PO history and is outside ordinary plant inventory until release. Planners may also use a different availability scope from the warehouse. Ask which question each report answered before escalating a mismatch.

title: Read a goods movement from its reference and its destination
lead: A movement type describes a business event. To predict the quantity, value and documents, read it together with its reference, stock segment and account assignment.
sections: Start with the business event

A receipt puts material into a destination. An issue removes it for a purpose. A transfer changes where or how it is held. A standard 101 receipt referring to an external stock PO brings goods into the chosen stock bucket and updates that PO item’s history. The same movement number can occur with another reference, including a production order. A material document explains the inventory event. If the event changes values relevant to financial accounting, follow its accounting document to identify the accounts and amounts.
Reconstruct three movements

A plant starts with ten spare motors in store A and none in B. It receives four against a stock PO, transfers three from A to B using a standard one-step 311, and issues two from B to a cost centre using 201. With constant standard value 50 per motor, no price variance and one valuation area, plant inventory value moves from 500 to 700 at receipt, stays 700 on the storage-location transfer and falls to 600 at issue. The final plant total of twelve conceals three distinct business explanations.
Use the documents to test the explanation

Read the material document item for the posted unit, movement type, date, plant, both locations, special stock and original reference. Verify the order item and its account assignment before predicting the offsetting line. A maintenance team may call a movement a transfer even when the posting actually charged a cost centre. Ask which balance should increase, which should decrease and who should bear the cost. That answer determines what evidence belongs in the case.

title: A reservation, a warehouse pick and a posted goods issue
lead: A reservation describes a planned requirement. The material document records the quantity actually issued. Keeping the two events separate helps explain why an apparently allocated part still appears in stock.
sections: Read the requirement

An ECC reservation identifies a material, quantity, requirement date and destination such as a cost centre or an order. It may be entered manually or created by another application. Its planning effects depend on the planning and availability rules in use. Creating a reservation for a goods issue leaves physical inventory in place. A warehouse can stage a box on its floor before the user completes the issue posting, so the timing of the pick and posting can differ.
Work a partial withdrawal

There are 30 bearings on hand. Maintenance reserves twelve for a repair and the store initially issues seven with reference to that reservation. Physical unrestricted stock falls to 23 and seven units have been withdrawn against the reservation. Five remain to be supplied, assuming the final issue indicator is clear and the requirement is unchanged. An additional unreferenced issue of five may reduce stock to 18 while the original requirement continues to look open. Reconcile the order or cost centre as well as the material before concluding the reservation was fulfilled.
Investigate apparently unavailable stock

Read the required date, requested location, movement allowed status, withdrawal quantity and final issue indicator. Match the reservation item to the goods issue reference and the real recipient. Then check the location and batch where the warehouse staged the parts. A projected availability shortage can coexist with a positive physical balance when other requirements fall due. Changing the final issue indicator is a business decision about further supply. Preserve evidence of what was physically issued before closing a partially fulfilled request.

title: Trace a batch through receipt, storage and consumption
lead: A batch distinguishes a lot of a material. Its identity, recorded properties and stock balance answer different questions during a traceability investigation.
sections: Separate identification from quantity

A batch-managed material can have several batches at one location, each with its own quantity. Plant or material scope of a batch identity depends on configured batch level. Read the material and organizational context alongside a printed batch number. Classification can hold characteristics such as grade or measured potency. Quantities are established from the stock records and material documents. A grade written in a characteristic supplies evidence about a lot, while a goods movement explains where quantities went.
Rebuild a delivery split

Suppose 120 bags of material M arrive in one truck, 70 from batch A and 50 from batch B. The receiver records two batch quantities. A later cost-centre issue of 80 comprises 60 from A and 20 from B. The remaining balance is ten from A and 30 from B. If the supplier reports a concern affecting A, the plant can identify the remaining ten and trace the 60 issued by reading the document items and recipients for A. A total of 40 remaining gives no answer about exposure.
Establish the evidence boundary

Compare the supplier lot and internal batch identifiers, receipt date, stock category, storage location and units. An external lot identifier may be shared across documents or use a different spelling. Document the link using the supplier delivery evidence. If a balance is zero, the batch can still have master data and a movement history. When two plants appear to share a batch, check the configured scope and material first. Do a chronological reconstruction at the requested cutoff date instead of inferring earlier movements from today’s stock alone.

title: Explain why batch determination chose a later-expiring lot
lead: Automatic batch determination combines strategy selection, eligibility, ranking and available quantity. A sort rule only affects batches that reached the ranked candidate list.
sections: Rebuild the selection

Identify the application, movement and organizational combination for which SAP searches. A search procedure and its strategies lead to a valid condition record. The strategy can specify characteristic restrictions, a sort rule and batch split behavior. First determine which strategy and date apply. Then examine classifications and stock availability for candidates. The configured batch level and the plant or storage location in the movement can change the population that the strategy sees.
Work a shelf-life example

Assume today is 1 June, an issue requires at least 20 days of remaining shelf life, all other characteristics match, and the strategy sorts eligible batches by earliest expiry. Batch A expires on 10 June and has 40 pieces. Batch B expires on 25 June and has 12. Batch C expires on 20 July and has 25. For a demand of 20, A fails the life requirement. If splits are permitted and both remaining batches are available, the proposal can take twelve from B and eight from C. The oldest physical stock was correctly excluded.
Find the first failed gate

Capture the exact requirement date, condition key, record validity, selection-class values, stock type and available batch quantities. In the selection analysis, distinguish a batch absent from the candidate list from one present but ranked later. Test one variable at a time in QA. Adjusting a sort direction will not admit a batch filtered by a characteristic. Increasing the available balance will not correct a missing strategy record. Record local overrides and whether the posted batch was manually selected.

title: Resolve a count difference using a trustworthy cutoff
lead: A physical inventory document compares a count at a defined point with a book quantity. A recount, a zero count and an unentered count are different pieces of evidence.
sections: Establish the comparison population

Specify material, location, batch, stock type and any special-stock owner. Set the planned count date and decide how operations will handle movements during counting. A posting block can prevent relevant goods movements. Freezing book inventory captures a comparison quantity in the inventory document. Those controls have different jobs. Freezing a number does not move a pallet or stop a forklift. The counting team needs a physical cutoff it can reproduce as well as consistent system timing.
Follow a delivery across the cutoff

At 09:00 the frozen book quantity is 100 and the team counts 97 in the agreed area. At 10:00 a receipt of 20 is posted and physically arrives. The live stock display now reads 120 before differences. The valid comparison for that count is 97 against 100, a shortage of three. After the correctly approved difference is posted, the live quantity becomes 117. Comparing the earlier count with 120 would falsely suggest a shortage of 23. A receipt physically counted before the cutoff but posted later requires a different reconstruction.
Check before posting differences

Get both the physical arrival time and SAP posting details, including entry time and posting date. Check unit conversions, the counted stock category, recount documents and transfers in adjoining locations. Use an explicit zero count when nothing was found. A blank can mean the count is pending. Investigate significant differences before authorizing posting. For valuated stock, posting a real inventory difference normally creates a value effect as well as a stock quantity change.

title: Reconcile the components held by a subcontractor
lead: Subcontracting separates three quantities: components you provide, components consumed by the processor, and finished assemblies you receive. Counting finished pieces alone cannot explain the supplier’s component balance.
sections: Identify what is still yours

A subcontract PO orders the finished material or assembly and lists the components expected for its manufacture. When your own components are provided to the vendor, the corresponding special-stock balance records your material at that vendor. Sending components changes where the stock is held. Consumption is normally recorded with the subcontract receipt. A vendor invoice covers the subcontract service according to the PO. Keep component units, finished-product units and service price units separate.
Work a component reconciliation

The subcontractor starts with ten seals owned by your plant. You send 90 more. The assembly uses two seals each, and you receive 30 assemblies. Planned consumption at receipt is 60 seals, leaving 40 at the vendor. The processor reports five additional seals consumed and provides a scrap record. When that extra consumption is substantiated and posted as a subsequent adjustment, the balance becomes 35. The receipt quantity of 30 assemblies remains correct. A shipment of five replacement seals would be an additional provision and would increase the vendor balance again.
Distinguish an adjustment from a return

Check plant, subcontractor, component material, batch and posting period. Reconcile all provisions, receipt-linked consumptions, returns of unused components and subsequent adjustments at the same cutoff. Supplier stock is generally a vendor-level pool for a component, so allocations to individual POs need documentary support. A later receipt reversal can undo its component consumption. Match reversals to their originals, and ask whether the vendor physically used, retained or returned the disputed quantity before choosing the corrective business event.

title: Track consignment from physical receipt to settlement
lead: Supplier consignment separates physical custody, ownership and liability. The useful question is when the company withdrew or took ownership of the supplier’s goods.
sections: Observe the ownership boundary

A receipt into supplier consignment adds stock identified with the supplier. The supplier still owns those units. Their physical presence in your warehouse does not yet represent the ordinary purchase of company inventory. A withdrawal for consumption or a transfer from consignment into your own stock creates a liability at the relevant consignment price. A subsequent settlement can convert the accumulated withdrawal liabilities into a supplier payable. Bank payment follows the payable and its payment terms.
Follow one delivery

Assume 50 seals arrive on consignment at an agreed price of 8 per seal, with no tax, price difference or rounding in this example. Ten are transferred into company-owned inventory. Supplier-owned quantity becomes 40, owned quantity rises by ten, and the withdrawal represents 80 payable through consignment settlement. Settlement of those ten clears the corresponding 80 from the consignment liability account and credits the vendor account. There is no reason to settle the 40 pieces still owned by the supplier merely because they arrived on the same delivery note.
Reconcile a vendor enquiry

Gather material, vendor, plant, agreement price and validity, withdrawal reference, posting date and settlement status. Distinguish a physical return of supplier-owned units from reversal of a withdrawal already settled. Determine which document existed before attempting either correction. If direct consumption was posted, expect the appropriate expense or receiving object rather than an increase in company inventory. The price unit in the consignment info record matters as well: a price per hundred pieces must be converted before checking a ten-piece settlement.

title: Who owns the next action on an open stock transport order?
lead: A stock transport order documents a requirement between plants. In a two-step process, issue and receipt occur separately and the difference is the quantity to investigate in transit.
sections: Identify the route first

In a classic intracompany stock transport order without a shipping delivery, the issuing plant can post goods issue with movement 351 and the receiving plant can post a 101 receipt with reference to the order. Transit bridges the two steps. A delivery-based route has additional shipping documents and can use different movement types. Cross-company routes can involve billing and invoice verification. Identify the actual design from the source documents before using a movement-type list as a reconciliation rule.
Follow partial deliveries

Plant A is asked to send 100 units to Plant B. It issues 60 today, then B receives only 45. At that point 15 of the 60 issued are in transit and 40 have not yet been issued. If A later ships the remaining 40 and B receives another 50, five remain in transit. The outstanding ordered quantity after the first receipt was 55, yet only 15 were physically in the shipping chain according to the posted documents. That distinction changes which team should investigate.
Check the last confirmed handover

Pair issue and receipt history by STO number, item, material, base unit and posting date. Check reversals, batches and receipt against the correct STO when a truck contains multiple orders. Ask the supplying plant for dispatch proof for the issued quantity and the receiving plant for unloading records. A delayed posting can produce a positive transit balance even after the goods arrive. Compare the same cutoff before escalating a physical loss, especially at period end.

title: Choose between cancelling a receipt and returning goods
lead: Two postings can both reduce stock by four pieces while describing different real events. Choose the event from the physical and documentary history.
sections: Decide which fact needs correction

A cancellation corrects an erroneous posting, such as a receipt entered twice for a single delivery. A return delivery records goods physically sent back after a genuine receipt, for example for a defect. A returns PO item supports a purchasing-led return process when that is how the business conducts the return. In classic examples, 102 reverses a 101 receipt, 122 records a return delivery and 161 is a returns PO movement. The allowed reference and follow-on documents depend on the route.
Use equal numbers to expose the difference

A shipment of ten valves arrives. In case A the receiver mistakenly posts fourteen. The purchasing record should ultimately reflect one genuine delivery of ten, with the posting error corrected using the permitted reference and quantities. In case B fourteen really arrived and four were found defective and returned the next day. Net stock can also be ten. The supplier-performance story in B includes an actual defect and return shipment. Record the return reason and retain the relationship to the original receipt.
Trace finance and ownership

Read the receipt, order history, stock type, batch, invoice status and any return or credit memo before posting. An existing invoice can constrain reversal, particularly with GR-based invoice verification. Reversing a goods receipt does not itself cancel the supplier invoice. A credit memo changes financial history and may require a separate document. Reconcile quantities and values after the approved correction, keeping original document numbers visible. If the warehouse cannot show whether the four pieces ever arrived, investigate that fact first.

title: One goods issue, three views: stock, financial account and cost centre
lead: A maintenance team takes spare parts from the store. The storekeeper asks how many remain, Finance asks which expense account was charged, and the cost-centre manager asks whose budget absorbed the cost. The three questions refer to one event but need different evidence.
sections: Translate the business event

Assume classic ECC, own valuated stock, a standard price of 12 per piece, one company-code currency and no price change. The maintenance department withdraws three pieces. The material document records the movement type, quantity, material, plant and storage location. The accounting document identifies the inventory account and the offsetting consumption account. On the cost side, inspect the actual account assignment on the expense line. A cost centre identifies responsibility for consumption. The G/L account classifies the expense by nature. Two cost centres can therefore receive charges to the same expense account.
Read the three answers together

With fifty pieces initially in stock, three issued leaves forty-seven. At the assumed price, the carrying amount removed is 36. On the accounting lines, that means a credit of 36 to stock and a debit of 36 to consumption. Suppose the accounts and amount match expectations but the cost centre is Maintenance West rather than Maintenance East. The evidence points to the recipient entered or derived on the movement. Changing the G/L mapping would redirect the expense classification for other movements while leaving the incorrect recipient unexplained.
Classify the discrepancy before proposing a fix

If the quantity is wrong, investigate the unit, the original movement and possible reversals. If the quantity and recipient agree but the account is unexpected, examine valuation class, the applicable transaction and account modifier, and the client mapping with FI. If the account and quantity agree but the amount differs, check price control, valuation area and posting date. An unresolved exception should name the questionable document line and the evidence that would resolve it.

title: Trace a third-party sale through purchasing
lead: A supplier delivers directly to a customer. Sales sees customer demand, Purchasing sees a vendor commitment, and Accounts Payable sees the supplier invoice. The strongest reconciliation key is the linked document item and its schedule, even when several items have the same material and quantity.
sections: Find the demand behind the order

In a classic third-party sales process the sales item and its schedule can create purchase requisition demand. Purchasing can convert that demand into a purchase order for direct delivery. Start with the sales item and the required delivery quantities by date. Follow each referenced requisition item into the vendor order. A changed date, split schedule or separate requisition for another customer can make a simple search by material and vendor give a plausible but incorrect answer. Inspect the ship-to information as well as the supplying vendor.
Work through a split delivery

A customer orders twelve pumps, with eight due in May and four in June. The consultant finds an order for eight and reports that four units are missing. The sales item shows two schedules. The first requisition was converted; the second is still open. The aggregate twelve units of demand reconcile when the two purchasing statuses are kept separate. The outstanding business task is to source the June requirement. Creating an additional twelve-unit order would duplicate the first commitment.
Locate the point where responsibility changes

A supplier acknowledgment establishes what the supplier promises, while a supplier invoice establishes what the supplier is charging. Neither alone proves the customer accepted the goods. Ask Sales which delivery evidence and billing basis its item category requires and check the actual document flow for this client. If only eight units have been invoiced by the vendor, trace the remaining four to their schedule before changing sales billing settings. Close the investigation by recording the purchasing owner, the open quantity and the business event still expected.

title: When a production confirmation and component issue disagree
lead: A production order can reserve components, the warehouse can stage them, and the system can post consumption. These are three distinct events. A production confirmation is useful evidence, but its existence alone does not establish the quantity of every component actually issued.
sections: Read the component requirement in the order

Inspect the component list and reservation of the particular production order. Check the required quantity, operation assignment, unit of measure, issue storage location and backflush indicator. An order retains its own component context. Today’s bill of material is a useful comparison but cannot by itself establish the expected withdrawal for an existing order. For a manually issued component, the withdrawal is recorded with reference to the order or reservation. A backflushed component can be issued during confirmation, depending on the order and confirmation settings.
Explain a short withdrawal

An order calls for two washers per assembly. Assume a confirmation for twenty good assemblies with zero scrap, no substitutions and exact proportional consumption. Forty washers are expected. The order shows one posted withdrawal of thirty-two. Before suggesting a manual issue of eight, check earlier partial confirmations, reversals and outstanding goods movement errors. Staged stock on a trolley is also a physical observation; it does not establish a posted withdrawal. If the remaining eight belong to a failed automatic movement, a manual posting and a later reprocessing could charge the order twice.
Agree who completes the exception

Ask Production to verify the confirmed quantity and Warehouse to verify the component actually used. Save the material document references and the error or confirmation reference. After the agreed correction, reconcile the signed component withdrawals again. If the real requirement was thirty-two because the remaining assemblies used a substitute, document the substitution and the corresponding order change. The appropriate outcome is a traceable match with production facts, rather than a mechanically closed reservation.

title: The goods arrived. Why can production use only part of them?
lead: A purchase-order receipt can update inventory while an inspection process controls how much becomes available for ordinary issue. Reading the material document and inspection lot together prevents two common mistakes: treating all physical stock as usable, and assuming that an accepted lot means every unit entered unrestricted stock.
sections: Follow the actual inspection route

For this example assume an active procurement inspection and a stock-relevant inspection lot. Find the material document item for the receipt, its stock type and any linked inspection lot. Check the material and plant, batch if relevant, and the lot quantity. Inspect results and the usage decision. The usage decision records the quality disposition; its associated stock postings show the quantities and destinations. The allowed routes depend on the inspection settings, lot status and the client process. A receipt without a stock-relevant lot follows a different investigation.
Reconcile the quantities

A warehouse receives one hundred units to quality inspection. The lot disposition sends ninety units to unrestricted stock, eight to blocked stock, and accounts for two through sample consumption. Under those assumptions the original hundred are fully explained. A production shortage report for ten units is consistent with the quality outcome even though the warehouse physically accepted a hundred. Before deciding that the PO was short delivered, compare the destination postings and any later issues of the unrestricted ninety.
Choose a correction that preserves the evidence

If the disposition was entered but stock is still in inspection, inspect the lot quantity left to post and the actual stock documents. If the unrestricted balance later fell, follow movements after the decision. A generic transfer proposed solely to make production stock available can conceal the inspection history. The quality owner should confirm the approved destination, and the warehouse owner should verify the resulting stock category, location and batch after the authorized posting.

title: Design a configuration change around its real scope
lead: A request such as “use the repair expense account at Plant East” contains a business distinction, not yet a configuration design. A successful test for one material proves only that case. First establish which combination of accounting inputs SAP can distinguish and which other transactions share it.
sections: Translate the requested distinction into keys

Obtain a correctly posted example and the example that should change. Record the company code and chart of accounts, valuation area and grouping if enabled, material valuation class, movement type, and the transaction and modifier for the expense line. Not every key uses every dimension. A receiver such as a cost centre can distinguish reporting responsibility while the automatic account determination rule still returns the same expense G/L. Compare the actual keys used with the proposed business boundary.
Try to disprove the proposed change

East and West currently share the same valuation grouping and valuation class for repair spares, with the same relevant GBB modifier. In this case, changing that shared row affects both sites. A successful posting at East cannot justify closing the change. Select a West material with the same keys and an East material with a different class. These two control cases distinguish a genuinely plant-specific result from a broad redirection or an unrelated material difference.
Write a decision Finance can review

One alternative is to retain the expense account and satisfy the requirement through cost-object reporting, if that meets the accounting policy. Another may require a reviewed configuration distinction with wider implications. For each alternative, identify future transactions affected, master data changes, test populations and ownership. An account change affects future determination; treatment of historical postings is a separate accounting decision. Save the signed-off examples and expected accounts, so the next consultant can tell which part of the business rule was intentional.

title: Reconstruct a purchasing incident from signed item history
lead: When Operations says ten units are missing, first decide which balance is in dispute. Ordered, received, invoiced, physically present and available-to-issue quantities answer different questions. A chronology at purchase-order item level lets the team agree on the facts before anyone proposes a correction.
sections: Set the grain, unit and time boundary

Record the purchase order number and item, base or order unit and conversion, and the posting-date cut-off used by the original report. Retrieve the material document number, year, item, movement type, signed quantity and reference for each relevant receipt or reversal. List invoice items separately. Reconcile quantities before bringing prices and currencies into the analysis. Sorting by document number alone can put late entries in a misleading sequence. Preserve entry time if the question concerns when the warehouse desk actually recorded an event.
Reconcile a misleading match

A PO for one hundred pieces has an eighty-piece receipt, followed by a ten-piece reversal linked to the receipt. The supplier has invoiced eighty pieces. Net received is seventy, thirty are still undelivered on the simple quantity comparison, and the invoice exceeds net receipts by ten. Comparing only the original eighty-piece receipt to the invoice would conceal the reversal. Record the reversal reason and ask whether a corrected goods receipt or supplier adjustment was expected. A quantity gap alone does not establish a payment block; inspect the actual invoice status and applicable tolerance.
Conclude with evidence that can change the answer

If the reversal is dated after the report cut-off, prepare both the as-of and current picture. If a further ten appears against another item, confirm the physical delivery reference with Warehouse before proposing a transfer between items. A strong incident note identifies the last agreed event, the first unexplained change and the person who owns the missing evidence.

title: From an internal request to an orderable requirement
lead: A requisition expresses demand at item level. The key design choice is what the requester knows and what Purchasing must still determine. Quantity, timing, receiving plant and the purpose of consumption are distinct decisions. Approval authorizes the request under the client’s rules. It does not tell you that a vendor has received an order.
sections: Follow a worked case

A maintenance planner requests twelve seals for the store and a one-off inspection costing 600 for cost centre M100. For the seals, identify the material, plant, unit and required date. For the inspection, capture a usable specification, service period and cost assignment. A buyer may source the two requirements separately. If an order covers eight of the twelve seals, four remain outside that order. An estimated PR price supports planning; the supplier’s negotiated PO conditions determine the order price.
How to investigate

When someone says an approved PR disappeared, display the original item and inspect its release status, assigned source, processing status, deletion or closure indicators and follow-on references. Compare those values with the filters in the buyer’s worklist. A closed item and a fully converted item may both disappear from an open list for different reasons. Preserve the requisition number and item even when several orders cover it.

title: Make two supplier quotations genuinely comparable
lead: A request for quotation fixes the buying question. Each vendor can answer in a different currency, price unit, delivery period or freight arrangement. A comparison only becomes meaningful after these differences are made explicit. The purchasing decision should remain understandable when a colleague revisits it months later.
sections: Follow a worked case

You request 600 seals to one plant by the same date. A offers 8.50 each with 240 freight for the order. B offers 87 per ten with freight included. At the requested quantity, in one currency with no taxes or rebates, A costs 5,340 and B costs 5,220. If B offers a three-week lead time and the plant needs them in one week, that cost advantage of 120 does not settle the delivery question. Document the schedule risk separately so the award can be explained.
How to investigate

Keep the common specification, quantity, unit, destination and requested date in each invitation. Retain the vendor-specific RFQ references and collective number where used. Record each response in quotation maintenance before comparing it. Investigate a missing line by distinguishing an unquoted item from an item quoted at zero. If offers use different currencies, record the rate and comparison date. Recompute manually when a condition is outside the comparison basis.

title: What is consumed when you release against a contract?
lead: An outline agreement records commercial terms for future calls. A quantity contract expresses the target in a unit. A value contract expresses it in money. A reference to the agreement on the order item makes release documentation useful; a supplier name shared by two documents proves little on its own.

A buyer agrees to 1,000 filters for the year at an illustrative 10 per filter. Two referenced orders call for 250 and 300. The target comparison is 550 released and 450 remaining before amendments. If only 400 have been received, the agreement and warehouse are measuring different events. On a 10,000 value contract, use the relevant release values and currency instead. A mixed-material agreement may reach its value target without any meaningful common total in pieces.
How to investigate

Compare the agreement validity interval, purchasing organization, item reference and release documentation. Look for cancelled or changed order quantities before treating a spreadsheet total as final. Check whether the buyer copied the price manually into a standalone PO. It may look economically similar yet leave no release reference. Reproduce target-exceeded messaging in the client before promising that a target acts as a hard cap.

title: Diagnose an unexpected source of supply
lead: An eligible vendor and the vendor selected for the next requirement are different questions. Eligibility depends on the material, plant, date and relevant source records. Selection can also depend on allocation history. A buyer who checks only the percentage column in a quota arrangement can easily predict the wrong result.
sections: Follow a worked case

Consider two eligible sources in the same quota period with no base quantity. A has quota 60 and 120 units already allocated. B has quota 40 and 40 units allocated. Fix the comparison date and procurement context first. Inspect validity, source-list blocks, agreement items and quota usage. lead: A price on a PO may be composed of several condition lines. To reproduce it, identify each condition’s basis, scale, currency, quantity unit and validity date. The order in which the calculation schema applies a percentage matters if freight or another amount is included in its base.

Use the saved conditions and their analysis. Establish whether a line came from a master condition, an agreement, manual entry or a reference document. title: Separate physical quantity, inventory value and purchase cost
lead: Three ledgers can describe the same purchase: physical units, the value of inventory on the balance sheet, and the cost assigned to a consuming object. The material type’s quantity and value update settings by valuation area influence the first two. The purchase purpose, account assignment and receipt valuation determine when a cost is recognized.

Compare three purchases of ten units at 20 each. For ordinary valuated stock at a compatible price, a valuated receipt adds ten units and 200 inventory value. For a quantity-managed, non-valuated material procured against a cost centre, a valuated receipt can add ten units and charge 200 to consumption without building inventory value. If the permitted order instead specifies a non-valuated GR, receipt still records the applicable quantity or delivery history and purchase cost is generally recognized at invoice. The timing of the expense is a separate decision from inventory value updating.

title: Why two materials reach different inventory accounts

title: Reconstruct both sides of an automatic goods posting
lead: In a typical valuated stock receipt the inventory line and the clearing line express different business events. Inventory posting uses BSX; GR/IR uses WRX. A price difference may add PRD. title: Trace a receipt under standard and moving average price
lead: Price control determines how a valuated material absorbs price differences. Standard price holds a predetermined unit valuation in the simple receipt case. Moving average price derives from stock value divided by stock quantity, considering the maintained price unit. An invoice posted after stock has been issued can introduce a second valuation question.

Opening stock is ten pieces at 10 each. Receive another ten at a PO price of 14. Ignore tax, freight and currencies. At standard price 10, inventory rises by 100 and the excess 40 goes to a difference account. With moving average price the receipt adds 140 to the original stock value of 100. Closing value is 240 for twenty pieces, or 12 each. Issuing five immediately afterward consumes 50 or 60 respectively. The same supplier price can therefore produce different inventory and consumption values.
How to investigate

To reproduce a historical posting, record the transaction order, valuation area and type, price unit, currency and pre-posting stock. A material master displaying today’s MAP cannot reconstruct last week’s issue without movement history. Reversals, returns, exchange differences and negative stock can complicate the simple weighted-average example. Determine which event first changed the valuation.

title: Why part of an invoice difference goes to inventory and part to expense
lead: A moving-average material can absorb an invoice price variance into the remaining valuated stock. When only part of the invoiced quantity is covered, part of the variance may go to the price-difference account. The quantity used in this check is the relevant stock coverage at the posting event. sections: Follow a worked case

Assume one plant valuation, one currency, no tax, no other stock and no reversals. Receive 100 pieces at 10, then issue 70 at 10. Remaining stock is 30 pieces valued at 300. An invoice for all 100 at 12 creates a price variance of 200. In this simple proportional case, 30/100 can be absorbed by inventory: 60. The other 140 goes to price differences. Remaining inventory becomes 360 for 30 pieces, a MAP of 12. With all 100 still on hand, the full 200 could be absorbed. With zero remaining, none could.

In the invoice simulation or accounting document, separate the GR/IR clearing amount of 1,000 from the additional 200. Compare actual stocks immediately before invoice, price control, valuation type, price unit and posting period. title: Design a test that can tell you which rule changed
lead: A useful regression test makes two competing explanations predict different results. A single successful document shows one path worked. A matched pair can show which condition mattered. Define the release, client settings, units, data owner and posting sequence so a colleague can reproduce the distinction.
sections: Follow a worked case

A team enables GR-based IV for a pilot supplier. A tester receives the entire order and invoices once. That proves little about matching individual deliveries. Instead create comparable items for six and four pieces received on different dates. Test the individual delivery references, partial invoices and a reversal after an invoice under the client’s settings. Record which documents are proposed and what remains open after each event. Include a control item using the existing invoice procedure.

title: Explain the same event across two reporting periods
lead: Posting date determines the period in which the material and accounting events are recorded, subject to the applicable MM and FI controls. title: Choose a credit memo, subsequent credit or invoice cancellation
lead: Three different facts can cause a supplier credit: fewer invoiced units, an agreed price reduction for units already invoiced, or a document that should never have been posted. These require different histories. A supplier credit note is evidence from the vendor; the business event determines the correct invoice-verification treatment.
sections: Follow a worked case

A supplier invoices ten units at 50. If two invoiced units must be credited in quantity and value, a quantity-related credit memo for two at 50 reduces the net invoiced quantity. If all ten remain valid and the supplier grants a rebate of 30 for the lot, a subsequent credit can reduce value while retaining the already invoiced quantity. If the original invoice was posted against the wrong vendor or document entirely, follow the approved cancellation and replacement process and examine its accounting consequences.

Trace the invoice number, PO item, goods receipts and any returns separately. A commercial credit does not prove that a physical return occurred. topic: Freight account determination without a material master
title: Freight cost in a K purchase order without a material code or valuation class
lead: SAP may allow the purchase order to be created, but a valuated goods receipt can fail if SAP cannot determine the freight clearing G/L account. Account assignment K provides the expense account and cost center; it does not replace automatic account determination for clearing accounts.
sections: Scenario

Account assignment: K (Cost Center). Material code: blank. Material group: Office Supplies. Material group valuation class: blank. Material cost: RM 1,000. Planned freight cost: RM 100. Assume the freight condition uses accrual key FR1, the GR Non-Valuated indicator is not ticked, and the full quantity is received. Assume no matching blank valuation class entry exists in OBYC.
1. During ME21N (PO creation)

With no material code, SAP checks the valuation class assigned to the material group. If it is not maintained, SAP uses a blank valuation class. For the expense G/L proposal, SAP normally checks GBB with the account modification associated with K. If the required entry is missing, SAP cannot automatically propose that expense G/L. You may manually enter a valid expense G/L and cost center and save the PO, provided all other checks pass.
2. During MIGO (goods receipt)

SAP attempts to debit the expense G/L in the PO with RM 1,100, credit GR/IR Clearing (WRX) with RM 1,000 and credit Freight Clearing (FR1) with RM 100, as shown in the example table. SAP must determine the clearing accounts separately. If FR1 requires a valuation class and there is no matching entry for a blank class, the goods receipt fails with an account determination error. The same problem can occur with WRX if its rules require that valuation class and no matching entry exists. These are attempted postings, not a posted accounting document.
Important configuration distinction

The missing blank valuation class alone does not guarantee an error. If FR1 does not use valuation class as a determination criterion and has a valid G/L for the relevant chart of accounts and other active criteria, freight account determination can succeed. If the condition is not configured as a planned delivery cost with FR1, or GR is non-valuated, the timing and accounting entries can differ.
3. How to resolve it

Option 1: Assign an appropriate valuation class to the material group, in Purchasing → Material Master → Entry Aid for Items Without a Material Master, and verify the corresponding OBYC entries.
Option 2: Maintain a matching blank valuation class entry with a valid G/L account for the applicable OBYC transaction keys.
Option 3: Configure FR1 independently of valuation class if that meets the business requirement. Review with Finance before changing shared account determination rules.
In summary

Account assignment K supplies the expense G/L and cost center. The freight condition determines the relevant clearing transaction key via the calculation schema. Even if the expense G/L is entered manually in the PO, SAP still needs valid OBYC settings for any clearing accounts required at posting. Check the exact key and account determination combination in the error message.
